title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Assessment: Special Parallelogram Properties
description: Show mastery by applying rectangle, square, and rhombus properties to classification, comparison, and measure problems.

questions.question: A parallelogram has four right angles but not all sides are congruent. What is the most precise classification?
questions.explanation: Four right angles make the parallelogram a rectangle. Without all sides congruent, it is not a square or rhombus.

questions.question: A parallelogram has four congruent sides but its angles are not right angles. What is the most precise classification?
questions.explanation: Four congruent sides make the parallelogram a rhombus. Since the angles are not right angles, it is not a square.

questions.question: The diagonals of every rectangle are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Rectangle diagonals are congruent and bisect each other, but they are not usually perpendicular.

questions.question: The diagonals of every rhombus bisect opposite angles.
questions.explanation: Rhombus diagonals bisect opposite angles as well as bisecting each other.

questions.question: In square ABCD, diagonals AC and BD intersect at E. If AE = 11 cm, what is BD?
questions.explanation: E is the midpoint of AC, so AC = 22 cm. Square diagonals are congruent, so BD = 22 cm.

questions.question: A rhombus diagonal bisects an angle into two 47-degree angles. The original whole angle measures ______ degrees.
questions.explanation: The diagonal creates two equal angle parts, so 47 + 47 = 94 degrees.

questions.question: Which statement is always true for both rectangles and rhombuses?
questions.explanation: Both are parallelograms, and all parallelograms have diagonals that bisect each other.

questions.question: A parallelogram that is both a rectangle and a rhombus is a ______.
questions.explanation: A square has the right-angle property of a rectangle and the all-sides-congruent property of a rhombus.

questions.question: A student says, "All rhombuses are squares because all rhombuses have equal sides." Correct the reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: Equal sides are not enough to make a square. A rhombus becomes a square only when it also has four right angles.
questions.explanation: A square requires both rhombus properties and rectangle properties.

questions.question: Explain why square diagonals are both congruent and perpendicular.
questions.correctAnswer: A square is a rectangle, so its diagonals are congruent. A square is also a rhombus, so its diagonals are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: The strongest way to reason about square diagonals is to combine rectangle and rhombus properties.
